data.body:
RCA + fix (confirmed at runtime).

MECHANISM (confirmed): the materialization fetch bounds ELAPSED wall-clock via subprocess.run(timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT=300) at two network sites — git_fetch.fetch_origin (src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py:341) and the --no-filter --refetch in repo_snapshot (src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:409). An HONEST large/cold-store transfer keeps clearing the low-speed floor (http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime), so the throughput-keyed stall-abort never fires, yet the fixed 300s wall clock cuts it off -> SnapshotFetchError 'timed out after 300s (attested mode fails closed)', a verdict-less FAULT. The scoped-fetch (Gerrit 2178) and present-full-SHA short-circuit (2180) reduce how often the transfer is large, but the fixed-cap fail-closed mode remains for any honest >300s transfer (cold/partial clone, or large backlog since last fetch). Residual defect CONFIRMED present after those merges: on current origin/main the fetch timeout was still hardcoded 300 at both sites.

Reproduced RED then GREEN in tests/unit/test_snapshot_fetch_timeout_configurable_8d34.py: asserted the effective timeout handed to the child (never elapsed time), so it fails under the fixed 300 cap and passes only once the ceiling is configurable/scaled — distinct from the stall-abort path in test_snapshot_fetch_stall_abort_12e4.py.

FIX (AC: 'the ceiling is configurable / scaled'): the wall-clock is now a GENEROUS, TUNABLE backstop, not the primary guard. Added git_fetch.fetch_timeout() resolving REBAR_SNAPSHOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS over a scaled default (_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600) via the owned config seam (config.resolve_fetch_timeout, live per call), used at both materialization-fetch sites AND the tightly-coupled sibling init.py cold tickets-branch fetch (which cited the same _GIT_TIMEOUT=300 cold precedent and shared the identical fail-closed exposure). The throughput-keyed stall-abort remains the guard against a wedged remote (trips a dead connection in seconds regardless of this ceiling). Portable: the knob is a plain env var / config, no CI-provider dependency; quick LOCAL git ops keep the 300s _GIT_TIMEOUT.

caused_by: 747f-d1ba-dd43-43f4 (commit 96a0d5c3f2fa '747f: fetch blobs in one RPC before materializing'), which introduced the fixed _GIT_TIMEOUT=300 materialization-fetch cap.
